title: Hydrogen-like spectrum explorer
question: How do level choice and nuclear mass change linked transition energy, cyclic frequency, and vacuum wavelength in the stated model?
predictionPrompt: For the selected transition, use the finite-proton reduced-mass factor below one to predict whether its wavelength is longer, shorter, or unchanged relative to the same infinite-mass state.
sourceRevision: CODATA 2022 adjustment; SI Brochure 2026 update; OpenStax University Physics Volume 3, 2016 web edition accessed 2026-07-27; Tour contract 2026-07-26
sourceLocator: R_inf, electron/proton masses, exact h and c, OpenStax sections 6.4, 8.1, and 8.5, and Chapter 7 model limits
caveats: A listed level difference is not a claim that a transition is allowed, strong, or observed.
The proton-mass option is physically specific to hydrogen and only illustrative when atomic number exceeds one.

numericalMethod.name: Bounded hydrogen-like Rydberg evaluation
numericalMethod.description: Evaluates the reduced-mass Rydberg level difference and linked photon identities with finite deterministic arithmetic.

modelComponents.label: Hydrogen-like level-difference model
modelComponents.description: Uses a nonrelativistic one-electron point-Coulomb Rydberg relation for bounded atomic number and principal levels.

attribution.sourceRevision: CODATA 2022 R_inf; OpenStax University Physics Volume 3, 2016 web edition accessed 2026-07-27; Tour contract 2026-07-26
attribution.sourceLocator: Rydberg relation, OpenStax sections 6.4 and 8.1, and Chapter 7 Hamiltonian boundary
caveats: The engine directly evaluates the conventional result rather than solving the Hamiltonian.

modelComponents.label: Electron-nucleus reduced-mass option
modelComponents.description: Uses either the infinite-nuclear-mass limit or the CODATA electron-proton reduced-mass factor.

caveats: No isotope catalog or higher-order recoil correction is included.

modelComponents.label: Linked photon representations
modelComponents.description: Maps one selected level difference to energy, cyclic frequency, and vacuum wavelength with exact International System of Units (SI) h and c.

attribution.sourceLocator: Fixed h and c and E = h nu = h c/lambda
caveats: The representations are dependent outputs, not separate observations.

equations: mu/m_e = 1 for infinite nuclear mass, or m_p/(m_p + m_e) for the proton model
nu = c/lambda; E = h nu = h c/lambda
assumptions: The system is a one-electron point-Coulomb ion represented by the nonrelativistic Bohr/Rydberg baseline.
Atomic number is an integer from 1 through 10, upper principal level is 2 through 12, and lower level is an integer satisfying 1 <= n_lower < n_upper.
The finite nucleus option always uses the proton mass; for atomic number above one this is illustrative rather than isotope-realistic.
Wavelength is in vacuum and the visible classification uses the conventional 380-750 nm interval.
Selection rules, line strength, fine and hyperfine structure, Lamb shift, broadening, calibration, and uncertainty are omitted.

controls.label: Atomic number
controls.description: Sets the nuclear charge number Z for the bounded one-electron model.
controls.playfulPrompt: Keep Z at one for ordinary hydrogen; higher values are hydrogen-like ions.

controls.label: Upper principal level
controls.description: Selects integer n_upper from 2 through 12 for the downward level difference.
controls.playfulPrompt: Choose where the electron starts in the model.

controls.label: Lower principal level
controls.description: Selects integer n_lower from 1 through 11; a valid state must keep it below n_upper.
controls.playfulPrompt: Choose the lower landing level and keep it below the upper level.

controls.label: Nuclear-mass model
controls.description: Selects the engine's infinite-mass limit or finite proton reduced-mass option.
controls.playfulPrompt: Let the proton move, then compare with an immovable nucleus.

options.label: Infinite nuclear mass
options.description: sets the reduced-mass factor to one

options.label: Finite proton mass
options.description: uses CODATA electron and proton masses

presets.label: Balmer-alpha
presets.description: Hydrogen Z=1, n=3 to n=2, with the finite proton reduced-mass correction.
presets.inspectionPrompt: Predict whether its wavelength is slightly longer than the infinite-mass result.

presets.label: Lyman-alpha
presets.description: Hydrogen Z=1, n=2 to n=1, with the finite proton reduced-mass correction.
presets.inspectionPrompt: Will this line fall in the visible or ultraviolet region?

presets.label: Balmer-alpha, infinite nucleus
presets.description: The same 3 to 2 level difference with nuclear recoil omitted.
presets.inspectionPrompt: Compare only compatible outputs and identify the reduced-mass shift direction.

outputSchema.label: Reduced-mass factor
outputSchema.description: mu/m_e, equal to one for infinite nuclear mass and below one for the proton option.

outputSchema.label: Effective Rydberg value
outputSchema.description: R_inf multiplied by the selected reduced-mass factor.

outputSchema.label: Transition energy
outputSchema.description: Positive model level difference in joules.

outputSchema.label: Transition energy
outputSchema.description: The same transition energy represented in electron volts.

outputSchema.label: Cyclic frequency
outputSchema.description: Photon cyclic frequency derived from the selected level difference.

outputSchema.label: Vacuum wavelength
outputSchema.description: The same vacuum wavelength represented in nanometres.

outputSchema.label: Spectral series
outputSchema.description: Lyman, Balmer, or Paschen when n_lower is 1, 2, or 3; otherwise no named series.

outputSchema.label: Spectral region
outputSchema.description: Conventional x-ray, ultraviolet, visible, or infrared classification from vacuum wavelength.

outputSchema.label: Visible interval
outputSchema.description: True only for the conventional 380-750 nm interval.

comparison.incompatibleBehavior: Render parallel model findings without merging lines or calculating residuals when compatibility keys differ.

visualization.description: Shows bounded principal levels, the selected downward transition, its spectral marker, and linked model values.

alternatives.description: A sentence states Z, transition, nuclear-mass option, series, region, energy, cyclic frequency, vacuum wavelength, and model caveats.
A table lists at most 11 lines sharing the selected lower level with transition, series, energy, cyclic frequency, vacuum wavelength, region, and visibility.

visualization.reducedMotionBehavior: Render the selected level arrow and spectral marker immediately without animated photon or level motion.

finding.changed: At runtime, the selected levels, atomic number, and nuclear-mass option determine one linked transition result and a bounded same-lower-level series table.
finding.cause: The hydrogen-like Rydberg level difference scales with Z^2 and the selected electron-nucleus reduced-mass factor.
finding.equation: 1/lambda = R_inf (mu/m_e) Z^2 (1/n_lower^2 - 1/n_upper^2); E = h nu = h c/lambda
assumptions: Integer engine bounds and n_lower below n_upper
Vacuum wavelength and conventional visible interval
finding.establishes: For an evaluated valid state, the model links the selected level difference to energy, cyclic frequency, vacuum wavelength, series label, and spectral region.
finding.doesNotEstablish: That the transition is allowed, strong, or observed; that a line identifies a unique atom; that the model is empirically validated; or that dimensional analysis replaces a bound-state Hamiltonian.
finding.sourceRevision: CODATA 2022; SI Brochure 2026 update; OpenStax University Physics Volume 3, 2016 web edition accessed 2026-07-27; Tour contract 2026-07-26
finding.sourceLocator: Atomic spectrum equations, inputs, outputs, OpenStax sections 6.4, 8.1, and 8.5, and Chapter 7 limits
caveats: Selection rules and transition strengths are not represented.
Fine structure, hyperfine structure, Lamb shift, finite size, external fields, broadening, and medium response are omitted.
No spectrum dataset, calibration, uncertainty propagation, or competing-model comparison is evaluated.
